mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average signals an active monetary easing policy that reduces the risk-free rate, thereby increasing the present value of future equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns following a decline in FEDFUNDS (relative to 12-month MA) are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that typically precedes corporate earnings deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE > 6.0%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases (or the average return is not significantly negative, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a contraction in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate revenues.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both HOUST and RSAFS are below their 3-month moving averages, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.02 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average signals an impending supply shock that reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, the 20-day forward returns following an INDPRO decline below 6-month MA are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer spending trend, as measured by a 3-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS), directly boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns following a 3-month rise in RSAFS are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers a hawkish monetary policy response, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases (or the average return is not significantly negative, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% and a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 100,000 monthly additions signals a severe labor market contraction that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both UNRATE > 5.5% and PAYEMS < 100000, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.02 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a consumer-driven expansion, a surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 970 (thousands of units) signals strong household confidence and increased spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the consumer-driven expansion regime, the 20-day forward returns following a HOUST surge above 970 are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.
